patterns.label: Name the concrete role
patterns.rule: Mention the exact job title and company early. Do not say 'a role at your company'.

patterns.label: One real hook from their words
patterns.rule: If a quote or About line is provided, reference at most one short phrase that appears verbatim in the research. Never invent a post, podcast, or shared history.

patterns.label: One soft ask
patterns.rule: End with one low-pressure ask: a short chat, a referral, or whether the team is still hiring for this role. Not a demand.

patterns.label: Short and human
patterns.rule: Gmail body under 120 words. LinkedIn note under 300 characters. No buzzword stacks, no 'I hope this email finds you well', no fake warmth.

patterns.label: Fit over flattery
patterns.rule: For recruiters and hiring managers, tie one skill from the CV to one requirement from the job. Do not praise the company in generic terms.

patterns.label: Referral path
patterns.rule: For employees and executives, ask whether they know who owns hiring for the role, or if a referral is appropriate. Do not pitch as if they posted the job unless evidence says they did.
